title: Definition of I (part a) likely unfaithful: path MI vs. transfer entropy

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
Definition 'I' sets $I=\mathcal I(X_{[0,\tau]};Y)$ using the FULL trajectory (incl. times after each measurement). Eq. (Ichain) $I=\sum_k \mathcal I(X_{[0,\tau]};Y_k\mid Y^{<k})$ is then claimed to be 'exactly the transfer-entropy-type sum'.

This is not transfer entropy: directed information / transfer entropy is causal, conditioning on the PAST and using the state at/before measurement time, whereas $\mathcal I(X_{[0,\tau]};Y_k\mid Y^{<k})$ contains anticipatory correlations with the future trajectory $X_{>t_k}$. The framework second law for repeated/continuous feedback (Sagawa-Ueda 2012; Horowitz-Esposito 2014; Ito-Sagawa 2013) is established with the transfer entropy, not the symmetric path MI.

Either the definition is unfaithful to the $I$ for which the second law holds, or the solver must PROVE path-MI = transfer-entropy for this model. Neither is done; the entire (b),(c) program inherits this.
